articles.summary: Quaest: veja como está a disputa pelo Senado na BA
articles.body:
Rui Costa (PT), Jaques Wagner (PT), João Roma (PL) e Angelo Coronel (Republicanos) — Foto: Reprodução/Divulgação; Divulgação; Alessandro Dantas/Senado; Divulgação/Senado

Pesquisa Quaest divulgada nesta quinta-feira (24) mostra como está a disputa pelo Senado na Bahia. O levantamento foi encomendado pela TV Bahia.

Em 2026, serão eleitos dois senadores em cada estado e no Distrito Federal, para renovar 54 das 81 cadeiras. Por isso, cada eleitor precisa votar em dois candidatos diferentes. Não é possível escolher o mesmo nome duas vezes.

A Quaest ouviu 900 pessoas de 16 anos ou mais entre os dias 20 e 23 de setembro. A margem de erro é de 3 pontos percentuais, para mais ou para menos, e o nível de confiança é de 95%. O número de registro no TSE é BA-01850/2026.

Na pesquisa espontânea da Quaest — em que os nomes não são mostrados aos eleitores entrevistados —, 71% (eram 85% em 27 de agosto) estão indecisos, porque não souberam citar um candidato.

Já na pesquisa estimulada , a lista de candidatos é mostrada, e cada entrevistado precisa responder duas vezes em quem pretende votar: para a primeira vaga e, depois, para a segunda vaga.

Os resultados da pesquisa para o Senado consideram as menções para a primeira e a segunda vagas em um total que soma 100% das intenções de voto e mantém a proporção entre candidatos, brancos/nulos e indecisos. Veja os números abaixo:

articles.title: Flávio Bolsonaro, candidato do PL à Presidência, faz campanha no interior de Minas | G1
articles.standfirst: Candidato disse que pretende investir em infraestrutura para movimentar a economia e facilitar a comercialização dos produtos do estado.
articles.summary: Candidato disse que pretende investir em infraestrutura para movimentar a economia e facilitar a comercialização dos produtos do estado.
articles.body:
O candidato Flávio Bolsonaro , do PL , fez campanha no interior de Minas.

Flávio Bolsonaro falou com a imprensa no meio da tarde no aeroporto. Disse que pretende investir em infraestrutura para movimentar a economia e facilitar a comercialização dos produtos do estado.

"Minas Gerais tem muitas vocações, desde o agro até o turismo. E a principal, sem sombra de dúvidas, é a mineração. Minas Gerais tem aquilo que o mundo inteiro precisa hoje, que são terras raras. Tem aqui um grande futuro promissor pela frente, com investimento na qualificação de pessoas para trabalharem nessa área, investimento em infraestrutura também para escoamento da produção do nosso agro e dos nossos minérios”.

No início da noite, Flávio Bolsonaro chegou a Teófilo Otoni. Foi recebido por apoiadores na Praça do Imigrante, no Centro da cidade. Flávio subiu em um trio elétrico acompanhado de candidatos do Partido Liberal e discursou para os eleitores.

De Teófilo Otoni, o candidato seguiu para Governador Valadares, no Vale do Rio Doce, para um encontro com apoiadores.

O g1 promove nesta sexta-feira (25) um debate com candidatos ao Senado pelo por São Paulo.

O encontro será nos estúdios da TV Globo na capital paulista, às 13h, com mediação da jornalista Ana Paula Campos.

O debate é parte de uma série realizada pelo g1 com os nomes que disputam o cargo de senador em oito estados e no DF ( veja mais abaixo ).

A iniciativa busca ampliar o espaço para a discussão de propostas e contribuir para que os eleitores conheçam os concorrentes. Em outubro, o eleitor poderá votar em dois nomes para o Senado.

O debate com os candidatos ao Senado por São Paulo poderá ser acompanhado pelo g1 e pelos perfis do portal nas redes sociais:

O g1 convidou os candidatos de partidos e federações com representação mínima de cinco parlamentares no Congresso Nacional. Também estariam aptos a participar os candidatos dos demais partidos que alcançassem cinco pontos ou mais na pesquisa Datafolha divulgada nesta quinta-feira (24) , mas nenhum atingiu esse percentual.

Os encontros terão como objetivo aprofundar as propostas dos candidatos e priorizar temas de interesse da população.

Os participantes ficarão posicionados em uma mesa redonda ao lado do mediador e terão 15 minutos de fala para administrar ao longo da discussão.

Seis temas serão previamente definidos e comunicados às campanhas antes do debate. A ordem dos assuntos será sorteada antes do início do encontro.

Os candidatos poderão solicitar a palavra dentro das regras estabelecidas, com intervenções de até 1 minuto e 30 segundos por vez .

articles.title: Judge dismisses Trump lawsuit against Iowa newspaper and pollster
articles.summary: WASHINGTON, Sept 23 (Reuters) - An Iowa judge on Wednesday dismissed President Donald Trump's lawsuit filed in late 2024 against the Des Moines Register news...
articles.body:
WASHINGTON, Sept 23 (Reuters) - An Iowa judge on Wednesday dismissed President Donald Trump's lawsuit filed in late 2024 against the Des Moines Register newspaper and ‌pollster J. Ann Selzer, saying a poll that showed the Republican leader trailing before the ‌2024 elections was legally protected speech.

Iowa District Judge Scott Beattie said Trump's lawsuit sought to stretch the law to turn speech ​that enjoys the highest category of legal protection under the Constitution into fraud.

"Ratings, forecasts, and predictions that reflect a subjective weighing of objective data points are not sufficiently factual to be susceptible to proof, and predicting uncertain future events is not an exact science for which a publisher may be held to account," ‌Beattie said.

Beattie said the lawsuit was ⁠barred by the First Amendment of the Constitution, which guarantees free speech and free press rights. He also ruled that Trump's lawsuit did not fit the state ⁠fraud statutes he sued under.

The ruling came as another judge appeared skeptical at a hearing that Trump's decision to ban CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House was legal, indicating he may rule against Trump ​in ​his latest clash with the media.

Trump sued the Register, ​its parent company Gannett and Selzer over ‌a poll ahead of the November 2024 election that showed Democratic presidential candidate Kamala Harris beating him in Iowa. He accused the newspaper and its longtime pollster of fraudulently misleading readers.

Free speech group FIRE, which represented Selzer, welcomed the ruling.

"We're pleased that the court recognized what we've said all along: This lawsuit was laughable from the beginning and never should have been brought," FIRE chief counsel Bob Corn-Revere said ‌in a statement.

A spokesman for Trump's personal legal team said ​he would appeal the ruling. He also said the Register and ​Gannett knowingly ran a "phony poll" in an "unlawful ​attempt to interfere in the 2024 presidential election and to defraud Americans into ‌believing" Kamala Harris was winning the race.

Trump won ​the election, including in Iowa.

Trump's ​pressure campaign against media coverage he dislikes has ramped up in his second term. He has repeatedly urged broadcasters to drop news programs he dislikes, called on the Federal Communications Commission ​to strip disfavored broadcast stations ‌of their licenses, filed several lawsuits against media outlets and banned some media outlets from ​the White House.

(Reporting by Kanishka Singh in Washington and Jack Queen in New York; ​editing by Donna Bryson, Chris Reese and Sonali Paul)

articles.title: MN Dem Sen candidate in hot seat over upcoming event hosted by man enveloped in fraud scandal: 'Red flags'
articles.summary: Peggy Flanagan's fundraiser is co-hosted by Minnesota's Medicaid Medical Director Nathan Chomilo, who served during the massive fraud scandal.
articles.body:
Minnesota Lt. Gov. and Democratic Senate candidate Peggy Flanagan is set to attend a fundraiser hosted by Dr. Nathan Chomilo, Minnesota's Medicaid medical director, during a time of Medicaid fraud scandal.

Chomilo, although not directly responsible for processing payments or overseeing program-integrity operations, has been associated with a scandal involving Medicaid-funded programs in Minnesota.

The optics of Flanagan associating with Chomilo, amid skepticism about her commitment to tackling fraud, have raised concerns among voters and political opponents.

Minnesota Lt. Gov. and Democratic Senate candidate Peggy Flanagan is set to attend a fundraiser hosted by an individual who has served as the state's Medicaid medical director during a time period where Medicaid fraud exploded onto the national scene.

Dr. Nathan Chomilo has served as Minnesota's Medicaid medical director since January 2020 and is listed as one of the hosts of an October 1 fundraiser supporting Flanagan, first reported by Townhall's Dustin Grage.

Much of Minnesota's broader fraud scandal has centered on Medicaid-funded programs, including autism services and Housing Stabilization Services, and although Chomilo was not the official responsible for processing payments, investigating fraud or overseeing the department's program-integrity operations, the optics of Flanagan associating with him is sparking skepticism about Flanagan's commitment to tackling the fraud issue.

"Apparently, the people who were supposed to be watching the money are too busy raising it for Peggy Flanagan," Grage posted on X . "This should raise some serious red flags."

"Things that make you go hmm… ," Chuck Darrell, former communications director at Minnesota Family Council posted on X.

"The number one thing going on with Minnesota's Medicaid program has been fraud over the last eight years of the Walz Flanagan administration ," Minnesota Republican State Rep. Kristin Robbins told Fox News Digital. "So he must have been aware. He must have known and clearly he had oversight responsibilities. He probably should have been held accountable for what was going on in the program and instead he's raising money for Penny Peggy Flanigan."

"It just shows her disdain for the taxpayers," Robbins, the chair of the last legislative session's Fraud Prevention and State Agency Oversight Policy Committee, continued, adding that Flanagan has "shown time and again disdain for Minnesotans who aren't on board with her radical agenda and this is just another example of that."

Chomilo was highlighted in an online profile in 2023, as warning signs were surfacing about potential Medicaid fraud in the state, as a healthcare professional who was focused on "incorporating community collaboration and racial equity into Minnesota's Medicaid policy development."

"Communities experiencing inequities in health and opportunity due to structural racism know what they need but often policymakers fail to incorporate their lived experience," Chomilo said. "By prioritizing policy development through a racial equity lens and implementing it through a community co-created process, Minnesota Medicaid is building racial equity into the core of the healthcare system."

On his LinkedIn page, Chomilo has called for ICE to be defunded, promoted a boycott of Target for ending DEI and lamented "Zionism in medicine today" in a recent Instagram post.

Robbins told Fox News Digital that "clearly" Flanagan is "aligning herself with the most radical wing of the Democratic Party on health care and that is what she will bring to the US Senate."

Nick Puglia, National Republican Senatorial Committee (NRSC) regional press secretary, told Fox News Digital in a statement, "Peggy Flanagan let fraudsters steal at least $9 billion from Minnesotans. Fundraising with those who perpetuated it is like handing lighter fluid to the arsonist who burned the house down."

Fox News Digital reached out to the Flanagan campaign and Chomilo's office for comment.

Polling shows that fraud is one of the top issues on the minds of voters heading into the November election, where Flanagan will face off against Republican Michele Tafoya.

Tafoya has consistently hit Flanagan on fraud, citing the Democrat serving alongside Walz as his top lieutenant since 2019 as the fraud scandal unfolded.

"I am appalled by the fraud that has occurred," Flanagan told Fox 9 Minneapolis in August.

"Minnesotans are upset about it. They're angry and I am too. I can tell you that this administration has taken steps. There's a new office of inspector general that was passed this last legislative session. We've added staff to the attorney general's office to root out Medicaid fraud. And, there was an aggressive action of shutting down a program that was being utilized by criminals. I think more absolutely needs to be done."

articles.title: Trump admin to end key part of arch review, effectively evading preservation law
articles.summary: The agency that oversees an important part of the National Historical Preservation Act says it will jettison a part of the approval process.
articles.body:
The Trump administration has said it will end a key part of a review assessing the impact of the president's proposed triumphal arch, effectively evading the federal historical preservation law that has been in place since 1966.

The analysis, known as a Section 106 review, usually requires independent groups that have an interest or expertise in historical preservation matters related to a project to sign off.

However, on Thursday, the Advisory Council on Historical Preservation, the federal agency charged with overseeing the review, said it would terminate the consulting process, essentially giving up on reaching an agreement.

In a letter to the Interior department announcing the move, it said it would instead invite the consulting parties to "participate in a meeting with the ACHP to verbally provide their comment" before asking the Interior secretary for "a final decision on the undertaking."

The change allows President Donald Trump's arch to bypass a significant hurdle in the approval process for getting built, but is almost certain to launch lawsuits over the legality of ending the review.

It also lays bare the administration's desire to fast track the project, blowing past objections from experts, legal questions and criticism from the public. The ACHP's move creates a glidepath to position the arch for final approval in early November.

The letter drew immediate criticism from multiple consulting parties, who told CNN they had not been given sufficient time to evaluate and give input.

"This truly is boundary busting, said Charles Birnbaum of the Cultural Landscape Foundation, a DC-based nonprofit which is among the parties. The administration's position that "somehow there has been a process is an outright lie," he said.

The consulting parties – a group of experts, state preservation officers and municipal authorities – were only given two meetings for the Section 106 review, a process that typically plays out over many months for projects of the size and scope of the arch. The most recent meeting, in early September, ended without an agreement as the parties said they needed more information.

Moreover, Trump's announcement this week that he intends for the arch to double as a "military complex," represents a significant change in the overall plan for the arch and necessitates more review, Birnbaum added.

Greg Werkheiser, attorney with Cultural Heritage Partners, PLLC, which has been involved in other lawsuits concerning proposed Trump projects, agreed.

"If we believe the president that he is turning his memorial arch into a military installation that stores ammunition and explosives, the Secretary of Interior will be permitting an entirely different project than the one the agencies and the public have been reviewing," he said. "That's a clear legal vulnerability."

Questions over compliance with Section 106 of the National Historical Preservation Act have been at the heart of legal challenges concerning numerous projects Trump has sought to push through, including his proposed construction of a " triumphal arch ," putting his name on the Kennedy Center, the renovation of the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool and his proposal to take over the public golf course at East Potomac Park .

The administration has tried to reshape the process by seeking to rewrite its requirements and stacking the ACHP with Trump-aligned members, CNN previously reported.

CNN has asked ACHP and the National Parks Service, to which the letter was addressed, for comment.

The next step now rests with Interior Secretary Doug Burgum, who is expected to receive a request for his approval from the ACHP by October 7. And with his anticipated greenlight, the arch would be up for a final approval before the National Capital Planning Commission, the last step before breaking ground.

This story has been updated with additional information.

articles.title: Trump's state dinner for Xi features sea bass and a long list of tech titans
articles.summary: A tech-heavy guest list, the fashion choices of those on it, who sat where and what was on the menu marked the softer — often and glitzier — details of diplo...
articles.body:
WASHINGTON (AP) — A tech-heavy guest list, the fashion choices of those on it, who sat where and what was on the menu marked the softer — often and glitzier — details of diplomacy as Donald Trump threw a Thursday night state dinner honoring China's leader Xi Jinping .

The event featured a cavalcade of billionaires, Washington powerbrokers, business leaders and the type of festivities that most excite Trump, who has a reputation for reveling in hosting parties.

"President Xi and I both understand we represent different systems, but the ties between our people endure, and we've never gotten along better," Trump said during his toast, adding that "together, we can continue to build a relationship that promotes prosperity and security for future generations."

Trump has done his best to impress Xi during China's leader's during Xi's three-day visit to Washington, and praised their close personal relationship — even as he has decried top Democratic candidates as "communists" ahead of the November midterm elections.

Xi and Trump discussed tensions over Taiwan , trade and artificial intelligence during business hours — even as an ongoing First Amendment fight over press access at the White House has unfolded. But Trump publicly chose to focus on showing Xi his White House updates on Thursday afternoon, including letting him tour his Marine One presidential helicopter and a new helipad he built for it — before attention quickly turned to the flashy details of the swanky meal.

Xi noted in his own toast that "President Trump has pledged to make America great again" and that "China is committed to achieving great national rejuvenation."

"These two goals are both ambitious and can surely be mutually reinforcing," Xi said.

Trump wore a tuxedo, and her office said first lady Melania Trump opted for a tuxedo-style outfit: a white Saint Laurent cotton poplin blouse, a black silk cummerbund and black brocade pants — both from Dolce & Gabbana — with a peony motif.

Xi chose a black suit and his wife, Peng Liyuan, wore a red gown. The East Room, where the dinner was held, featured low lighting and place settings with elegant red and gold decor.

Those in attendance included OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, who signed autographs upon arriving at the White House. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang opted for a tuxedo over his trademark black leather jacket. Bernard Arnault, the CEO of French luxury goods company LVMH, walked through black security fencing to enter the event.

Trump says he can't help but talk up the ballroom being built

The president toasted his strong relationship with Xi and the bond between the U.S. and China, but then added, "If I could go off script just for a second, I just want to say I had to do it," as those assembled laughed.

"I'd like to invite everyone in the room to visit through that beautiful curtain in the back," Trump said, referring to the construction site of his White House ballroom on the South Lawn, which he said, "you've heard so much about."

Trump said the project was a year from completion, and said he thought attendees "will see something that I think you will really love."

The president said that after the dinner attendees could go see the worksite and be "the first people to step foot" on it.

"We'll do that. Maybe after we've finished with the entertainment tonight," Trump said, asking, "Anybody wants to walk into a construction site that's nice and sparkling, it's our honor to have you do so."

Trump has called the ballroom he's building the "Great Hall of the United States," and suggested it could rival the Great Hall of the People, where he dined during a state visit to Beijing in May.

The president also presented Xi with an eagle statue that he said was designed "in personal collaboration with Melania and myself." Xi did not present Trump a public gift in return during the dinner.

The first lady helped craft the evening's menu, which was served on the red china from Ronald Reagan's presidency. It featured a first course of yellow squash velouté with wild mushrooms, fresh herbs, crispy pancetta and drizzled scallion oil.

After that, guests got sesame-crusted sea bass with braised baby bok choy, roasted garden eggplant and a sauce verte. Dessert was vanilla crémeux with sour cherry confit and walnut frangipane, as well as ice cream with honey from the White House.

Trump has sought to one-up Xi after Beijing

The dinner came after the president took the unusual step of personally greeting Xi and his wife on Wednesday as they arrived at Joint Base Andrews outside Washington. Normally, presidents wait for their state visit guests to arrive at the White House itself before offering a formal welcome.

Thursday's dinner was packed with technology industry titans like Amazon founder Jeff Bezos , Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk , Google and Alphabet CEO Sundar Pichai , OpenAI President and co-founder Greg Brockman, and Dell Technologies chairman and CEO Michael Dell .

During his own visit to Beijing in May, Xi hosted Trump for a state dinner that unfolded beneath grand chandeliers in the Great Hall of the People. That event also included many tech luminaries, such as Tim Cook , formerly Apple's CEO, and Musk.

It was all a stark departure from 2015, when then-President Barack Obama was preparing to host Xi for a state visit and Trump — in the midst of his first presidential run — criticized all the hubbub.

"Just take them to McDonald's and go back to the negotiating table," Trump said then, during a rally in South Carolina. He later conceded on Fox News Channel that Xi might at least be worthy of getting "probably a double-size Big Mac."

articles.title: New Trump-focused "Love Me" ad campaign paid for by taxpayers hits airwaves
articles.summary: Ads promoting President Trump and paid for by American taxpayers are now airing on network and national cable.
articles.body:
A new ad campaign glorifying President Trump is on the air on national cable and national networks including CBS beginning Thursday, and it's being paid for by American taxpayers.

The first ad, which hit the airwaves Wednesday and aired on Fox News Channel, opens with Mr. Trump vowing, "We will defeat communism, socialism and Marxism in America." Set over a soundtrack of JMSN's song "Love Me," flash-cut random shots from the president's second administration appear with text on screen. The photos show the president at rallies, pardoning turkeys, at the White House with Christmas decorations, standing with the FIFA trophy, surrounded by flags, flanked by military leaders, outside the Taj Mahal, and more.

The ad repeatedly flashes "America will never be a communist country" on screen and also touts his administration's tax cuts and other broad expressions of support for domestic manufacturing and law enforcement in text on screen. It ends with the voice of Dana White, CEO of the Ultimate Fighting Championship, declaring, "He's the toughest, most resilient (man) I've ever met and nothing was going to stop him from fighting so hard for the country he loves."

In a post on X , JMSN said he did not grant a license for the use of "Love Me."

"To anybody who has followed my career and knows what I stand for and built my career on, it should go without saying that I would never authorize my music to be used for ANY political agenda or campaign," he said, and he indicated that no one asked him for permission to use it.

The ad, which appeared Wednesday night during "Primetime with Jesse Watters" and on Thursday afternoon, contains an on-screen disclosure that it was "Paid for by the U.S. Government."

A second ad that recounts the U.S. capture of former Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro and his wife and features Mr. Trump and his top Cabinet officials aired on CBS stations and other networks Thursday evening. CBS News has learned that there are multiple versions of the ads, with some 30 seconds long and others 60 seconds. The U.S. government produced the content and paid for the air time through an ad agency.

The White House, in response to CBS News' inquiries about the pro-Trump ad, denied it was a political ad and called it a "public service announcement."

"These public service announcements are about reminding Americans to love their country and understand what makes it worth defending, at home, at our borders, and abroad," a White House spokesperson said. "The ad is educational and unapologetically patriotic. We should be proud of our country."

A White House official said the PSAs "are clearly not political," and noted, "The President is not on the ballot and the ads don't have a call to action."

Previous presidents have run PSAs, too. During the Biden administration, all of the living presidents except Mr. Trump appeared in a PSA to encourage Americans to obtain a COVID vaccination.

Democratic Sen. Maggie Hassan of New Hampshire wrote to White House chief of staff Susie Wiles to demand information about the cost of running the ad and said it "raises deep concerns about the Trump Administration's use of taxpayer dollars."

"The advertisement does not have a clear official government purpose and appears to run afoul of federal prohibitions against the use of appropriated funds as part of 'a general propaganda effort designed to aid a political party or candidates,'" Hassan wrote. She also asked the White House for information about the contractors involved, the source of the funding and whether funding was diverted from federal agencies in order to run the ad.

In another letter to Wiles, the top Democratic appropriators in the House and Senate demanded that the ad be immediately pulled from air, saying it was a violation of federal law.

"This is the sort of government propaganda one might expect in North Korea, not the United States of America, and it is an egregious and illegal misuse of Americans' hard-earned tax dollars," Sen. Patty Murray of Washington, Sen. Jack Reed of Rhode Island, Rep. Rosa DeLauro of Connecticut and Rep. Steny Hoyer of Maryland wrote.

Campaign finance experts said the commercial likely does not violate election law, even as it generated scrutiny on social media for appearing to be a campaign ad.

"It doesn't appear to be supporting or endorsing a candidate for public office," said Richard Briffault, a law professor at Columbia University. Briffault, however, agreed with Hassan that there are questions about whether it could violate the propaganda law.

Democratic Sen. Jacky Rosen of Nevada has a bill to ban political ads featuring cabinet members that are paid for with tax dollars. She is trying to introduce an amendment to it Thursday to address at least the look and content of this new Trump spot.

articles.title: VÍDEO: Como justificar ausência nas eleições? | G1
articles.standfirst: Eleitores que estiverem fora da cidade onde votam podem justificar a ausência sem sair de casa. Depois da eleição, as regras mudam. Série de vídeos do g1 explica as eleições de 2026, os cargos em disputa e tira dúvidas.
articles.summary: Eleitores que estiverem fora da cidade onde votam podem justificar a ausência sem sair de casa. Depois da eleição, as regras mudam. Série de vídeos do g1 explica as eleições de 2026, os cargos em disputa e tira dúvidas.
articles.body:
Vai estar fora da sua cidade no dia da eleição e não vai conseguir votar? Nesse caso, é possível justificar a ausência pelo aplicativo e-Título. Basta acessar a opção "Justificativa de Ausência" no menu do aplicativo. Quando a justificativa é feita no próprio dia da votação, não é necessário apresentar documentos que comprovem o motivo da falta.

Quem preferir também pode justificar presencialmente. Para isso, é preciso preencher o Requerimento de Justificativa Eleitoral (RJE) e apresentar um documento oficial com foto. O formulário pode ser retirado nos locais indicados pela Justiça Eleitoral ou impresso previamente pelos sites do TSE e dos tribunais regionais eleitorais.

📍 Em uma série de 50 vídeos , o g1 explica os principais temas das eleições de 2026. Os conteúdos mostram como funcionam as pesquisas, explicam o papel dos cargos em disputa e o funcionamento do Congresso, e trazem orientações práticas para votar. A série também aborda o impacto das novas tecnologias na campanha, como inteligência artificial, deepfakes e influenciadores.

Mas, se você deixar para resolver depois da eleição, as regras mudam. Nesse caso, será necessário informar o motivo da ausência e apresentar documentos que comprovem a justificativa. O pedido pode ser feito pelo e-Título ou pelo Autoatendimento Eleitoral, disponível no site do TSE.

Depois de enviar a solicitação, o eleitor recebe um protocolo para acompanhar a análise do pedido. Se a justificativa for aceita, a situação fica regularizada. Caso seja recusada, será necessário pagar multa pela ausência.

Também é importante ficar atento aos prazos: cada turno da eleição conta separadamente e tem seu próprio prazo para justificativa. Quem não votar no primeiro turno, em 4 de outubro, poderá justificar a ausência até 3 de dezembro. Já para quem faltar ao segundo turno, o prazo vai até 8 de janeiro.

articles.title: Quais os documentos que precisa para votar? | G1
articles.standfirst: Eleitor precisa apenas de um documento oficial com foto, mas deve saber qual zona e seção eleitoral em que vota; informações podem ser consultadas on-line no site do TSE.
articles.summary: Eleitor precisa apenas de um documento oficial com foto, mas deve saber qual zona e seção eleitoral em que vota; informações podem ser consultadas on-line no site do TSE.
articles.body:
Para votar, o eleitor precisa apenas de um documento oficial com foto, mas precisa saber qual sua zona e seção eleitoral. — Foto: Érico Andrade/G1

Para votar nas eleições de 2026, o eleitor deve apresentar um documento oficial com foto aos mesários . O título de eleitor em papel não é obrigatório e, na maioria dos casos, nem precisa ser levado.

Também é possível votar usando apenas o aplicativo e-Título , desde que ele exiba a fotografia do eleitor. Caso a versão digital não tenha foto, será necessário apresentar outro documento oficial com foto.

Quais documentos são aceitos para votar?

A Justiça Eleitoral aceita os seguintes documentos oficiais com foto para identificar o eleitor no dia da votação:

carteira de categoria profissional reconhecida por lei , como OAB, CRM, CREA e outros conselhos profissionais.

Mesmo que estejam vencidos, esses documentos podem ser aceitos, desde que permitam identificar o eleitor.

Já a certidão de nascimento e a certidão de casamento não são válidas para votar , pois não possuem fotografia.

É obrigatório levar o título de eleitor?

Não. O título de eleitor em papel não é exigido para votar. O documento serve apenas para facilitar a consulta da zona eleitoral e da seção onde o eleitor vota.

Se o eleitor souber o local de votação, basta apresentar um documento oficial com foto . Nem mesmo o e-Título é obrigatório, caso o eleitor saiba sua zona e seção eleitoral.

Sim, desde que a versão do aplicativo exiba a foto do eleitor. Nessa situação, o e-Título pode ser utilizado sozinho para a identificação na seção eleitoral, sem necessidade de apresentar outro documento.

Se o aplicativo não mostrar a fotografia — normalmente porque o eleitor ainda não fez o cadastro biométrico — será obrigatório apresentar também um documento oficial com foto (lista acima).

Quem vota no exterior precisa dos mesmos documentos. Brasileiros inscritos para votar no exterior também podem utilizar o e-Título. Da mesma forma, quando o aplicativo não exibe a fotografia, o eleitor deverá apresentar um documento oficial com foto para comprovar sua identidade.

Para evitar problemas na hora de votar, a recomendação é levar um dos documentos com fotos listados acima .

Caso não tenha o e-Título ou a versão impressa em mãos, o ideal é ir para o local de votação sabendo qual a zona e a seção eleitoral, que podem ser consultados no site do TSE ou nos portais dos tribunais regionais.

articles.summary: O debate Senado Piauí g1 acontece às 10h desta sexta-feira (25) com cinco candidatos confirmados para discutir temas como saúde, segurança e combate à seca.
articles.body:
Candidatos ao Senado pelo Piauí esperados para o debate promovido pelo g1 na sexta-feira (25). — Foto: g1

O g1 realiza, na sexta-feira (25), um debate com candidatos ao Senado pelo Piauí. O encontro acontecerá em um estúdio da Rede Clube, em Teresina , com mediação do jornalista Marcos Teixeira. A transmissão será ao vivo pelo g1 e pelos perfis do portal nas redes sociais do portal.

Conforme as regras do debate, foram convidados candidatos de partidos e federações com, no mínimo, cinco representantes no Congresso Nacional : Antônio Barros (Novo), Antônio José Lira (Avante), Ciro Nogueira (PP), Francinaldo Leão (PSOL), Jorge Lopes (PSDB), Júlio César (PSD), Marcelo Castro (MDB), Maria Madalena Nunes (PSOL) e Tiago Junqueira (PL).

Inicialmente, o g1 previa realizar dois debates, um às 11h e outro às 15h. A divisão foi necessária porque os encontros teriam limite de seis participantes.

Júlio César (PSD) e Marcelo Castro (MDB) recusaram o convite. Já Francinaldo Leão (PSOL), que havia confirmado presença, desistiu posteriormente. Com isso, os candidatos confirmados foram convidados a integrar um único debate, marcado para as 10h de sexta-feira (25).

A assessoria de Ciro Nogueira (PP), por sua vez, informou que o candidato não participará do encontro após a alteração no formato do evento.

Com isso, cinco candidatos são esperados para o debate: Antônio José Lira (Avante), Jorge Lopes (PSDB), Tiago Junqueira (PL), Antônio Barros (Novo) e Maria Madalena Nunes (PSOL).

O debate será transmitido ao vivo pelo g1 e pelos perfis do portal nas redes sociais:

O debate tem como objetivo aprofundar a discussão das propostas dos candidatos sobre temas de interesse da população.

Cada candidato terá 15 minutos para administrar ao longo do debate.

Além desse tempo, cada participante terá mais 1 minuto para as considerações finais.

Seis temas foram definidos previamente e informados às campanhas: incentivo ao turismo, combate à seca, saúde, trabalho e emprego, crime organizado e segurança pública.

A ordem dos temas será definida por sorteio antes do início do debate.

Os candidatos poderão solicitar a palavra para fazer intervenções de até 1 minuto e 30 segundos.

Não serão permitidas intervenções consecutivas do mesmo participante. Para voltar a falar, o candidato deverá aguardar a manifestação de outro concorrente.

O candidato que estiver com a palavra não poderá ser interrompido.

Em caso de insistência em falas simultâneas, a produção poderá cortar os microfones para que o mediador restabeleça a ordem.

Além do Piauí, o g1 já realizou debates com candidatos ao Senado em outros estados durante o mês de setembro. Veja a íntegra dos encontros:

articles.title: Conselho do MPF decide nesta sexta se abre investigação sobre atuação de Gonet no caso Master | G1
articles.standfirst: Órgão vai analisar se há elementos suficientes para aprofundar a apuração sobree referências de Vorcaro ao PGR em mensagens. Gonet apareceu em foto com banqueiro em Londres.
articles.summary: Órgão vai analisar se há elementos suficientes para aprofundar a apuração sobree referências de Vorcaro ao PGR em mensagens. Gonet apareceu em foto com banqueiro em Londres.
articles.body:
Procurador-Geral da República Paulo Gonet em sessão plenária extraordinária do STF — Foto: Rosinei Coutinho/STF

O Conselho Superior do Ministério Público Federal (CSMPF) decide nesta sexta-feira (25) se abre ou não uma apuração sobre possível crime envolvendo o procurador-geral da República, Paulo Gonet .

O Conselho vai avaliar a atuação de Gonet:

na condução de investigações sobre o banco;

na condução das apurações relativas ao Banco Master.

O caso é inédito no Conselho. Os nove integrantes vão analisar se as referências ao procurador-geral devem ser arquivadas ou se há elementos suficientes para aprofundar a apuração.

🔎 Se a maioria dos conselheiros entender que há indícios a serem investigados, um subprocurador-geral da República será designado para analisar os dados e verificar a possível existência de crime. Ao concluir a análise, o subprocurador apresentará um relatório ao Conselho. Se forem identificados indícios de crime, os fatos serão encaminhados ao Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF), que decidirá sobre a eventual abertura de um inquérito.

Desde a divulgação das primeiras menções a Gonet em julho, o procurador-geral da República vinha reunindo apoio de subprocuradores e também da base do MPF.

Mas a publicação da foto de Gonet, em uma confraternização ao lado do dono do Banco Master em Londres, no Reino Unido, mudou o cenário e fez o chefe do MPF ser alvo de duras críticas internamente.

Na foto, Vorcaro aparece sentado próximo a Gonet, que exibe um charuto nas mãos e em frente a uma mesa com copos de uísque. A imagem teria sido tirada em 2024 após a participação em um evento, mas foi enviada pelo advogado Ciro Soares em junho de 2025.

Aliados de Gonet dizem que, apesar das críticas e do desgaste, a maioria do Conselho deve votar pelo arquivamento do caso . Já os conselheiros mais críticos à atual gestão apostam que Gonet pode ser alvo ao menos de questionamentos na sessão.

A sessão será presidida pelo vice-presidente do Conselho Superior do MPF, subprocurador-geral da República Nicolao Dino. Gonet não deve comparecer, apesar de ser o presidente do Conselho.

O vice-PGR, Hindenburgo Chateaubriand, participa da votação. Após a abertura da reunião, fala o relator do procedimento, o subprocurador-geral da República Francisco Sanseverino.

Em seguida, será aberta a votação aos conselheiros, do mais novo para o mais antigo.

articles.title: TSE recebeu 45,4 mil denúncias sobre campanha eleitoral | G1
articles.standfirst: TSE soma 45,4 mil registros até esta quinta-feira (24). Principal alvo das denúncias, a propaganda nas ruas gera queixas sobre bandeiras que dificultam a passagem nas calçadas e avançam sobre ciclovias.
articles.summary: TSE soma 45,4 mil registros até esta quinta-feira (24). Principal alvo das denúncias, a propaganda nas ruas gera queixas sobre bandeiras que dificultam a passagem nas calçadas.
articles.body:
Candidatos a deputado estadual e federal são alvo de 69,2% das denúncias sobre a campanha eleitoral de 2026 registradas no Pardal, aplicativo do Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE). Entre os tipos de reclamação, lidera a propaganda em vias públicas, com relatos de materiais que atrapalham a passagem de pedestres, cadeirantes e ciclistas ( leia mais abaixo ).

Até quinta-feira (24), o sistema reunia 45.408 denúncias, das quais 31.428 envolviam candidaturas a esses dois cargos. As reclamações sobre propaganda em ruas e calçadas somavam 19.477, ou 42,9% do total, seguidas pelas categorias de bens particulares e bens públicos.

Segundo a representante do TSE Renata Martínez Talim Dias, os wind banners , bandeiras sustentadas por hastes e bases, aparecem com frequência nos relatos sobre vias públicas. As queixas envolvem estruturas que prejudicam a visibilidade no trânsito e ocupam espaços destinados à circulação.

❗ Os registros são relatos de possíveis irregularidades e não significam que houve infração comprovada. Segundo o TSE, uma mesma situação pode causar várias denúncias feitas por pessoas diferentes.

O total de 45.408 denúncias já é 17,2% maior que o registrado durante todo o primeiro turno de 2022 , quando o Pardal recebeu 38.747 relatos. Considerando os dois turnos daquele ano, foram 52.920 registros, volume superior ao balanço parcial de 2026. Em 2018, ao todo, foram 48.673 denúncias de irregularidades nas campanhas.

Denúncias registradas no Pardal nas eleições de 2018, 2022 e 2026; balanço deste ano é parcial, até 24 de setembro — Foto: Arte/g1

Por que candidaturas a deputado concentram os registros?

Quais são os tipos mais frequentes de denúncia?

Propaganda no caminho de pedestres e ciclistas

Publicação no X mostra denúncia registrada no Pardal sobre bandeiras de campanha mantidas em via pública após às 22h, horário limite para a exposição desse material — Foto: Reprodução/X

As candidaturas a deputado estadual são alvo de 16.810 denúncias, enquanto as de deputado federal aparecem em 14.618. Juntas, representam 69,2% dos registros. Na sequência estão as disputas para governador, com 5.899.

Pedro Gallotti, mestre em Direito do Estado pela Universidade Federal do Paraná (UFPR) e especialista em direito eleitoral, diz que a quantidade de candidaturas ajuda a explicar essa concentração. Há mais concorrentes aos cargos de deputado do que às disputas para senador, governador e presidente.

“Há milhares de campanhas simultâneas que ampliam a possibilidade de irregularidade nas propagandas, principalmente nas redes sociais”, afirma Gallotti.

Renata Dias ressalta, porém, que o TSE ainda não fez um estudo para explicar a distribuição dos registros entre os cargos. Segundo ela, a avaliação deve ocorrer depois do período eleitoral.

Veja os registros por cargo ou categoria:

Candidaturas a deputado estadual e federal concentram 69% das denúncias registradas no Pardal em 2026, até 24 de setembro — Foto: Arte/g1

Deputados distritais aparecem em uma categoria separada e não estão incluídos no cálculo dos 69,2%.

São Paulo concentra o maior número de denúncias, com 8.859 registros, seguido por Bahia, com 5.401, e Minas Gerais, com 3.928.

Propaganda em vias públicas lidera o balanço, com 19.477 registros. Na sequência aparecem bens particulares, com 5.320, e bens públicos, com 5.142.

Carro de som, minitrio e trio elétrico: 2.907;

Distribuição de material gráfico: 1.679;

Confecção, utilização ou distribuição de brindes: 739.

A classificação indica o assunto da denúncia, não uma conclusão da Justiça Eleitoral sobre o que ocorreu.

Enquanto a categoria de vias públicas envolve propaganda nos espaços de circulação, a de bens públicos pode incluir material colocado em postes, pontos de ônibus, sinalização de trânsito e passarelas.

Dias explica que algumas situações causam dúvidas na classificação, como a instalação de propaganda em canteiros próximos às ruas. A descrição e as imagens apresentadas ajudam a identificar o problema.

Já a categoria de bens particulares reúne relatos sobre propaganda em propriedades privadas.

Gallotti ressalta que locais privados abertos à população, como igrejas, cinemas e comércios, são considerados bens de uso comum para fins eleitorais e estão sujeitos à proibição de propaganda nesses espaços.

Nos bens particulares em que a divulgação é permitida, devem ser respeitados os formatos autorizados. “A propaganda deve ser espontânea e gratuita, ou seja, sem pagamento ao proprietário ou inquilino”, afirma.

Bandeiras que avançam sobre ciclovias, estruturas que dificultam a passagem de cadeirantes e bases deixadas nas calçadas estão entre os problemas relatados por cidadãos durante a campanha eleitoral.

Segundo Dias, do TSE, os wind banners são apontados com frequência nas reclamações por prejudicar a visibilidade no trânsito ou reduzir o espaço disponível para circular.

“Eles não colocam bem no meio da ciclovia, mas colocam na beiradinha da ciclovia e atrapalham a passagem, porque a ciclovia não é tão larga assim”, explica.

Relatos de cidadãos publicados nas redes sociais mostram como essas estruturas interferem no deslocamento. Em Serra Talhada (PE), um ciclista gravou um vídeo para reclamar de bandeiras eleitorais instaladas ao longo da ciclovia da Avenida Afonso Magalhães. Segundo ele, o material ocupa parte da faixa e prejudica a visão de quem pedala.

“As bandeiras estão ocupando parte do espaço da ciclovia e, principalmente, prejudicando a visão dos ciclistas”, afirma o cidadão.

Bandeiras de propaganda eleitoral avançam sobre o espaço de circulação de ciclistas — Foto: Reprodução

Em Governador Valadares (MG), um morador registrou bases de concreto com ferros expostos nas calçadas do bairro Santa Rita. Na publicação divulgada nas redes sociais, ele relata que as bandeiras foram recolhidas, mas as estruturas permaneceram no passeio.

“Aí vem o idoso, uma pessoa que vem andando distraída, não vê esse concreto aqui, mete o pé, cai, machuca”, reclama o cidadão no vídeo.

Base de concreto usada para sustentar bandeira de propaganda eleitoral é deixada na calçada — Foto: Reprodução

De acordo com a legislação eleitoral, a passagem precisa permanecer livre mesmo durante o horário permitido para a propaganda. A regulamentação prevê a colocação de mesas e bandeiras móveis nas vias públicas a partir das 6h e a retirada às 22h .

“Bandeiras e mesas devem ser móveis e não podem dificultar o trânsito de pessoas ou de veículos”, afirma Pedro Gallotti.

Segundo o especialista, essa exigência também vale para as estruturas que sustentam os wind banners : “Essas bases não podem ser fixadas, devem poder ser removidas a qualquer tempo."

Gallotti acrescenta que a concentração de muitas peças em um mesmo local pode ser considerada irregular pelo efeito visual semelhante ao de um outdoor.

“Identificada a irregularidade, a própria Justiça Eleitoral pode determinar a retirada ou a regularização da propaganda, conforme o seu poder de polícia”, explica o especialista.

A aplicação de multas depende da infração e do procedimento cabível . Consequências mais graves para a candidatura exigem apuração específica, como em situações que possam configurar abuso de poder econômico.

A divulgação por apoiadores também pode ocasionar responsabilidade para o candidato. Segundo Gallotti, isso pode ocorrer quando ele é notificado e não regulariza a propaganda ou quando as circunstâncias demonstram que sabia da divulgação.

“Também é possível responsabilizá-lo quando as circunstâncias concretas forem tais que seja impossível concluir que ele desconhecia a propaganda”, afirma.

“O objetivo do Pardal é cessar com a irregularidade”, resume Dias, representante do sistema de denúncias.

Segundo ela, os relatos são encaminhados, em geral, aos cartórios eleitorais responsáveis pela região . Denúncias sobre propaganda na internet também podem ser direcionadas a unidades específicas dos tribunais regionais eleitorais, conforme a organização de cada tribunal.

Os servidores verificam as informações e as provas apresentadas. Podem solicitar mais detalhes ao cidadão, realizar diligências e procurar a candidatura para que a propaganda seja retirada ou regularizada.

Quando o problema é resolvido, o registro pode ser arquivado. Conforme a gravidade da situação ou o descumprimento de uma determinação, o caso pode ser encaminhado ao Processo Judicial Eletrônico (PJe).

“Se realmente se constatar que é alguma coisa de fato mais grave ou que não cumpriu a determinação de retirada da propaganda, isso vira processo”, explica Dias.

Os registros encaminhados pelo Pardal são autuados na classe Notícia de Irregularidade de Propaganda Eleitoral. O envio ao PJe não significa, por si só, que houve crime ou condenação.

A partir dessa etapa, o acompanhamento passa a ser feito no sistema de processos. “O processamento é todo no PJe”, afirma a representante do TSE.

No balanço de 24 de setembro, as denúncias estavam distribuídas assim:

Notificação orienta eleitores a denunciar irregularidades pelo aplicativo Pardal, da Justiça Eleitoral — Foto: Reprodução/TSE

O Pardal recebe denúncias de propaganda eleitoral irregular nas ruas e na internet. O aplicativo é gratuito e está disponível para celulares Android e iPhone. Para registrar uma ocorrência, é necessário se identificar pelo gov.br ou pelo e-Título, mas a identidade do denunciante fica protegida por sigilo.

O cidadão deve descrever o que aconteceu e apresentar elementos que ajudem na análise, como fotos, vídeos, áudios ou links. Após o envio, recebe um protocolo para acompanhar o andamento pelo aplicativo ou pelo link encaminhado ao e-mail informado.

Pardal : propaganda eleitoral possivelmente irregular, como bandeiras que atrapalham a circulação, material instalado em locais proibidos e irregularidades na divulgação de candidaturas na internet.

Sistema de Alertas de Desinformação Eleitoral (Siade) : informações falsas sobre urnas, datas, horários e locais de votação, páginas que se passam pela Justiça Eleitoral e conteúdos que possam comprometer a integridade das eleições. Segundo o TSE, propaganda sem identificação e vídeos enganosos de candidatos devem ser comunicados pelo Pardal.

Ministério Público Eleitoral : suspeitas de crimes eleitorais e outros ilícitos que ultrapassem a fiscalização da propaganda. O próprio Pardal oferece direcionamento para esses canais quando o relato não se enquadra na finalidade do aplicativo.

Candidatos ao Senado pelo Amazonas: Eduardo Braga (MDB); Wilson Lima (União Brasil); Plínio Valério (PSDB); Isael Munduruku (Rede); Professora Evany (Psol); Capitão Alberto Neto (PL). — Foto: Reprodução

articles.title: Veja regras e como assistir debate com candidatos ao Senado do Acre | G1
articles.standfirst: É a primeira vez que emissora reúne postulantes a senadores para confronto de ideias. Encontro também será transmitido no g1 e Rádio CBN Amazônia Rio Branco.
articles.summary: É a primeira vez que a Rede Amazônica reúne postulantes a senadores para confronto de ideias. Encontro também será transmitido no g1 e rádio CBN Amazônia Rio Branco.
articles.body:
A Rede Amazônica Acre realiza nesta sexta-feira (25) um debate com os candidatos ao Senado às 20h55 (horário local), após a novela Quem Ama Cuida, com mediação do jornalista Fabiano Villela. ( Saiba como acompanhar ). Foram convidados todos os candidatos.

Além da TV, as discussões serão transmitidas ao vivo e em tempo real no g1 e na Rádio CBN Amazônia Rio Branco . Esta é a primeira vez que a emissora faz um debate entre os candidatos ao Senado.

A expectativa é que o momento seja uma oportunidade para que os candidatos ao cargo no legislativo federal também possam expor suas ideias e propostas. Em outubro, são dois votos para o Senado.

Candidatos ao Senado pelo Acre participam de debate da Rede Amazônica — Foto: g1 AC

Durante reunião na última sexta-feira (18) , foram apresentados o formato e as regras para a discussão, que devem ser baseadas em:

perguntas entre os candidatos, que serão sorteados durante o programa;

temas determinados e de interesse do eleitor.

articles.title: Jackson warns Supreme Court’s emergency rulings imposing ‘institutional costs’
articles.summary: Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson implored her Supreme Court colleagues Thursday to dip into emergency docket cases less frequently, warning that it is imposing “institutional costs.” “Why is it that one party should get a fast pass to the Supreme Court of the United States, when so many other parties are queued up, waiting patiently for…
articles.body:
Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson implored her Supreme Court colleagues Thursday to dip into emergency docket cases less frequently, warning that it is imposing “institutional costs.”

“Why is it that one party should get a fast pass to the Supreme Court of the United States, when so many other parties are queued up, waiting patiently for the court’s attention ?” Jackson told a crowd gathered at the University of the District of Columbia’s law school.

It’s the junior liberal justice’s latest public critique of her colleagues’ repeated decisions to step into ongoing litigation while it remains pending, oftentimes to allow President Trump to resume aspects of his agenda blocked by lower courts. Jackson has repeatedly said the interventions are having a potentially “corrosive” effect on the judiciary’s ordinary handling of cases.

Speaking on Thursday, Jackson suggested the nation’s highest court isn’t treating emergency cases like how it did when she was a clerk roughly 25 years ago. At that time, she said justices, unlike those today, tried to stay out of significant, controversial cases as long as possible.

“It has been noticeably less restrained, especially with respect to pending cases that involve controversial matters,” Jackson said.

She did not mention Trump by name as she delivered the university’s annual Joseph L. Rauh Jr. Lecture. But, at one point, Jackson invoked a 2025 dissent from fellow liberal Justice Sonia Sotomayor, in which she stated the Trump administration had the court’s emergency docket on “speed dial .”

Hours ahead of Jackson’s talk, the same case from this Sotomayor opinion returned to the Supreme Court . The administration again wants an emergency order to lift a judge’s permanent block on its third-country deportation policy.

Jackson herself received the case by default, as she handles emergency matters arising from Massachusetts — where the case was filed. She ordered a response by Monday but so far has declined to immediately step in.

It marks the Trump administration’s 40th emergency application to the Supreme Court since the president retook the White House. It’s a staggering number that the administration argues reflects lower judges’ frequent overstepping, while its critics say it shows the president has been acting lawlessly.

Jackson has repeatedly ruled against the Trump administration in its flood of emergency appeals. She has often penned searing dissents, standing alone at times.

“If we’re not careful, the emergency docket can and will become an end run around the standard review process, a special avenue that certain privileged litigants can use selectively,” Jackson said on Thursday.

Avila Chevalier, the Democratic nominee for New York's 13th Congressional District, was among dozens of demonstrators taken into custody after protesters blocked a roadway near the United Nations General Assembly meeting Thursday ahead of Netanyahu's address at the event. "Darializa was just arrested while peacefully protesting Netanyahu's speech at the United Nations," a Thursday afternoon post from the candidate's social media account said. "Our government has unlimited funds to arm a genocide against Palestinians but tells us there's nothing left to feed and house our own people. Stop arming Israel!" ISRAEL'S AMBASSADOR SAYS NYC’S MAMDANI IS ‘SOWING CHAOS’ AHEAD OF NETANYAHU’S UN APPEARANCE The demonstration Avila Chevalier was reportedly arrested at drew around 250 protesters to the corner of 1st Avenue and 39th Street in Manhattan, according to City & State New York. Police began making arrests after protesters sitting in the roadway refused to move. Avila Chevalier defended her participation following the arrest. "Netanyahu belongs at the Hague, not in the streets of New York City, and certainly not addressing the United Nations General Assembly," she said in a statement reported by Bloomberg. Avila Chevalier was not the only New York political figure taken into custody. City Council members Chi Ossé and Alexa Avilés were also arrested during the demonstration, according to City & State, while the Daily Mail reported actress Susan Sarandon was among those detained at the protest. Outlets reported that roughly 80 to 100 protesters who refused orders and remained at the demonstration were arrested. RISING SOCIALIST STARS ON TRACK TO CONGRESS: WHO ARE DARIALIZA AVILA CHEVALIER, BRAD LANDER AND CLAIRE VALDEZ? Avila Chevalier, 32, pulled off a major Democratic primary upset in June when she defeated five-term Democratic incumbent Rep. Adriano Espaillat in the heavily Democratic 13th District, which covers Upper Manhattan and parts of the Bronx. Fox News Digital previously reported that New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani endorsed Avila Chevalier in late May during an appearance on MS NOW, praising her commitment to working-class New Yorkers and saying he looked forward to fighting alongside her for their shared affordability agenda. She is a member of the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) and received backing from the group's New York City chapter during her congressional campaign. Avila Chevalier has been a prominent pro-Palestinian activist as well, with Fox News Digital previously reporting on how she led anti-Israel protests at Columbia University and said she helped launch Columbia University Apartheid Divest's (CUAD) boycott, divestment and sanctions campaign. articles.title: FBI says source of its jobs portal breach still unknown as hackers allege employee data compromised
articles.summary: ShinyHunters claims it stole FBI employees' names, addresses and Social Security numbers in a cyber attack targeting the FBIJobs.gov portal. An expert weighs in.
articles.body: The FBI is working to determine whether a breach involving its jobs website originated within the bureau or through a third-party provider after a criminal hacking group claimed it obtained FBI employees’ personal information. "The FBI is aware of a cyber-criminal enterprise group claiming a compromise of the FBIJobs.gov portal and alleged impact to FBI employee personally identifiable information (PII)," the organization wrote in an X post Thursday. "While the point of breach is still undetermined — whether a third-party or the FBI’s enterprise — we are actively and aggressively investigating this matter and working closely with those third-party providers that support FBIJobs.gov to mitigate any and all risk." Jason Pack, CEO of Media Rep Global Strategies and a retired FBI supervisory special agent, said the distinction between a personnel data breach and access to the FBI’s classified systems is critical as investigators determine the scope of the incident. FBI INVESTIGATES AFTER SHINYHUNTERS HACKERS CLAIM THEFT OF AGENTS' PERSONAL DATA "There is a meaningful difference between somebody obtaining personnel information and somebody gaining access to classified investigative systems," he told Fox News Digital. "Based on what we know right now, there is no indication they have the keys to the kingdom." ShinyHunters, a criminal hacking and extortion group, has taken responsibility for the breach and said it stole information belonging to nearly all FBI agents and people who applied to work for the bureau, Reuters previously reported. A sample of data shared with Reuters contained agents’ names, home addresses, Social Security numbers, assignments and, in some cases, names of family members, according to the outlet. DMV BREACH CONFIRMED AS HACKERS CLAIM 200,000 RECORDS STOLEN Pack said combining personal information with information about an FBI employee's work could create additional security risks. "If an adversary knows who somebody is, where they work and what they do, they can build a much more believable scam around that person," he said. Pack said assignment information could also carry counterintelligence implications if it falls into the hands of a foreign intelligence service. "There is also a counterintelligence concern. If a foreign intelligence service can associate particular people with certain assignments, it can help them identify individuals they may want to learn more about, approach or potentially assess for recruitment," he added. "That does not mean that is happening here. It simply explains why assignment information can have value to an adversary." CHINA-LINKED HACKERS INFILTRATED US GOVERNMENT NETWORKS BEFORE FBI TAKEDOWN Pack stressed that the hackers’ claims remain separate from what the FBI has confirmed, and said the bureau still needs to determine what information was accessed, how the breach occurred and who may have been affected. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "The danger from stolen personal information does not necessarily end when the computer vulnerability is fixed," he said. "Criminals may hold onto that information and use it weeks or months later." The FBI said it is working with third-party providers supporting FBIJobs.gov as investigators seek to determine the source of the breach and mitigate potential risks.

articles.title: Trump rolls out red carpets for Xi Jinping, though he has portrayed China as a global menace
articles.summary: Just two months ago, President Donald Trump gave a primetime speech accusing China of interfering in the 2020 election.
articles.body: WASHINGTON — He has accused China of hacking America’s elections and plundering its wealth, yet President Donald Trump has showered the visiting Chinese leader, Xi Jinping, with tributes and affection during their summit meeting this week at the White House. Trump met his Chinese counterpart on the tarmac at Joint Base Andrews, Maryland, outside Washington on Wednesday rather than wait back at the White House for an official greeting. It’s the first time he has ever shown a visiting world leader that courtesy. Trump rolled out a red carpet not once but twice for Xi. The leaders walked side by side down a 100-foot-long red carpet after Xi’s Air China plane landed at Andrews. Another red carpet was laid out Thursday morning when Xi and his wife, Peng Liyuan, arrived at the White House for the summit’s first full day. In the evening, Trump feted Xi at a state dinner whose menu included sesame-crusted sea bass and braised bok choy, followed by a dessert of vanilla crémeux and honey ice cream. “As the leaders of our two nations, President Xi and I both understand that we represent different systems, but the ties between our people endure, and we’ve never gotten along better since the first trade ships from New York left the harbor to arrive on the banks of the Pearl River,” Trump said at the dinner. He gave his guest a statue of a bald eagle as a gift. All the pomp and ceremony might appear unusual given Trump’s past complaints that China has meddled in elections and exploited the U.S. through trade. Just two months ago, Trump gave a rare primetime speech asserting that China interfered in the 2020 election, which he lost to Joe Biden. But Trump, who has long believed that personal relationships are key to managing geopolitical tensions, has set out to charm the Chinese leader. “From the time of my first election in 2016, President Xi and I have forged a friendship — a truly great friendship, actually — built on mutual respect and the vital interests of our people,” Trump said Thursday morning in joint public statements he and Xi made before they held a private meeting in the Oval Office. Xi struck a cordial tone in his remarks, saying he and Trump have developed a “personal rapport and stayed in touch.” He also made an announcement certain to delight American children and anyone who has ever logged on to a panda-cam feed for a respite from life’s pressures: China will soon send two giant pandas, Ping Ping and Fu Shang, to the Atlanta zoo, Xi said. In an unusual rebuke from a member of Trump’s own party, Sen. Roger Wicker, R-Miss., chairman of the Armed Services Committee, said Wednesday in a speech on the Senate floor that, “quite frankly, had the White House asked me for advice, I would have suggested the president not invite Xi Jinping to Washington for such a lavish welcome here in the United States of America, based on all of the troubling issues we have with President Xi and the Chinese Communist Party.” China may also have aided Iran in the war with the U.S. An F-15 fighter jet that was shot down over Iran in April was most likely hit by a Chinese-made shoulder-launched missile, three people familiar with the matter told NBC News. And in the early days of the seven-month-old conflict, China may have given Iran radar capabilities to help spot stealth aircraft, according to one of the people and a U.S. official with knowledge of the matter. Honoring the leader of the world’s largest communist country may also undercut an argument Trump has made to discredit Democrats in the midterm elections. He has warned repeatedly that Democratic candidates would steer the U.S. in a communist direction if they are elected. Sen. Lisa Murkowski, R-Alaska, told NBC News on Thursday, “I personally look at the red-carpet treatment and thought it was a little bit over the top.” Sen. John Kennedy, R-La., said in an interview that while he didn’t mind seeing Xi thrown a dinner, “I don’t think the president ought to believe his bull----.” After the U.S. and Israel launched attacks on Iran on Feb. 28, the Iranian regime exerted a chokehold over the Strait of Hormuz, a crucial shipping lane for oil supplies. Xi “could open up that strait with a phone call, and in a myriad of ways, he is helping Iran with military equipment, intelligence,” Kennedy said. “The guy learned to lie before he learned to talk.” China, which has criticized the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran and called for diplomatic negotiations, denies supplying Iran with weapons or military equipment. No substantive breakthroughs are expected at the summit, foreign policy experts said. The two presidents were set to discuss trade, the Iran war and artificial intelligence, among other issues that have divided the U.S. and China. Trump entered the summit in a weakened posture, experts said, vexed by the prolonged Iran war and looming midterm congressional elections in which his party could lose its slim majority. He lacks the leverage needed to wring concessions from China, experts said. Mark Montgomery, a retired Navy admiral, said at a pre-summit event hosted by the FDD think tank: “We have a president entering this playing a weak hand. I’m not 100% sure President Trump knows he’s playing a weak hand. I am 100% sure that leader Xi knows Trump is playing a weak hand.” One area of cooperation might be the creation of a hotline that the U.S. and China could use to cope with an emergency arising from rapidly evolving AI technology, Secretary of State Marco Rubio suggested in an interview on “Fox & Friends” this week. “It’s not a bad idea; it’s one that we’ll explore with the Chinese, among others,” Rubio said. Along with closed-door meetings, Trump made a point to show off his prized White House projects. He took Xi outside to see the helipad he built on the South Lawn. Both men pointed down at the granite base. When the leaders passed the press corps at one point, Trump said, “We had a great meeting.” He said Xi was “an expert on stone, aside from many other things, and he loves good granite.” Xi said nothing. Walking with Xi along the West Wing Colonnade, Trump pointed to his “Presidential Walk of Fame” — pictures and biographical accounts of former presidents. He paused at the portrait of Biden, showing how he has mocked Biden by referring to him as “Autopen,” the device that presidents have used when they don’t have time to sign their own names to documents. A video snippet released by the White House shows the two presidents chuckling at the picture of Biden, with Trump giving Xi a friendly pat on the arm. Confronting Xi in the moment may prove difficult for Trump. Xi is president for life; Trump is a president at risk of losing his governing majority in Congress. His approval rating has hit a second-term low. One source of Xi’s leverage is his hold over rare earth materials, which are used in high-tech manufacturing. Last year, Trump slapped China with steep tariffs, igniting a trade war. Trump has long complained that China’s trade policies have bled the U.S. of wealth. A statement from the White House in April 2025, tied to Trump’s “Liberation Day” tariffs, said Chinese practices “have given China global dominance in key manufacturing industries, decimating U.S. industry.” But China’s command of rare earth supplies has proved an effective countermeasure, a resource the Trump administration can’t afford to lose. The two sides agreed to a trade truce last year, and on Wednesday they agreed to extend it two months, from Nov. 10 to Jan. 10. Viewers who wanted to watch the summit live faced unusual difficulties following a media ban that Trump imposed last week. He barred CNN, MS NOW and Politico from entering the White House grounds, prompting them to sue to regain access. CNN is part of the five-network press “pool” that provides real-time coverage of the president’s public events. In solidarity with CNN and the other outlets that were banned, the other networks opted to suspend video pool coverage of Trump. Confusion reigned in the hours before Xi arrived. ABC News had been scheduled to provide the pooled video feed. A White House official hurriedly approached a network journalist and asked where the camera was. Absent any clarity over when the banned outlets’ access would be restored, ABC declined to record. Trump took notice that TV coverage had thinned. He wrote on social media that CNN and MS NOW “refused to cover one of the Biggest and Most Beautiful Events to take place in many years, the arrival at the White House of the Highly Respected President of China, Xi Jinping, and his beautiful wife, Madam Peng.” Journalists from both CNN and MS NOW were physically unable to cover Xi’s arrival at the White House. Though a federal judge had ruled overnight that their access must be restored, they were still barred from entering the White House until about two hours after Xi showed up. During a photo spray with Xi later in the day, Trump joked that China had the friendliest press corps, according to a press pool report. A Reporters Without Borders survey of press freedoms worldwide ranked China 178th out of 180 countries, sandwiched between North Korea and Iran.

articles.title: New Jersey Gov Mikie Sherrill calls on lieutenant governor to resign after sexual harassment investigation
articles.summary: New Jersey Gov. Mikie Sherrill gave Lt. Gov. Dale Caldwell a Friday deadline to resign after investigators substantiated sexual harassment and ethics violations.
articles.body: New Jersey Gov. Mikie Sherrill called on handpicked Lt. Gov. Dale Caldwell to resign by Friday after an independent investigation substantiated sexual harassment and two ethics violations. The investigation found Caldwell told a female staffer that "you young women are looking for young sperm" after she told him her younger friend was not interested in a romantic relationship with him. Investigators concluded the sexually charged remark constituted sexual harassment and said Caldwell's denial that he made the comment was not credible. The staffer said she subsequently attempted to distance herself from Caldwell at work and avoid traveling with him when possible. REPUBLICANS TIGHTEN SCREWS ON SHERRILL AS NONCITIZEN VOTER PROBE ENTERS NEW PHASE "I’m calling for his resignation and giving him until tomorrow to do so," Sherrill said Thursday, calling the substantiated sexual harassment finding "extremely troubling." The report also substantiated two ethics violations, finding Caldwell brought personal guests to ticketed events without advance ethics clearance or payment and repeatedly attempted to secure a promotion for a state employee with whom he had a romantic relationship. Investigators found Caldwell continued bringing unpaid guests to events despite repeated training and warnings, including on May 23, one day after he was formally notified of the investigation. SHERRILL ESCALATES TRUMP FIGHT OVER VOTER FIASCO DAY AFTER MULLIN PRAISES NJ COOPERATION Four days after receiving notice of the investigation, Caldwell also used his state email account to recommend his romantic partner for a leadership position in another executive branch department, referring to her as "my friend" and forwarding her resume and letter of interest. Investigators said Caldwell did not disclose their romantic relationship while advocating for her promotion. Caldwell denied wrongdoing in a May response to investigators, calling the allegations false and misleading and saying he believed the facts would exonerate him. He denied hitting on or asking women out while conducting official business. Fox News Digital reached out to Caldwell for comment on the report and Sherrill's resignation demand. Sherrill said the violations reflected "a pattern of behavior" that persisted despite warnings and training. "The lieutenant governor’s resignation is necessary and in the best interest of New Jersey residents," the Democrat said. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Sherrill also took aim at President Donald Trump in announcing her decision, saying the president "continues to undermine confidence in public service at the federal level" and that she would not accept "a culture that sweeps misconduct under the rug" in New Jersey. The investigation began after the state's chief ethics officer received an anonymous complaint in May alleging inappropriate behavior toward women and ethics violations. Caldwell was formally notified of the investigation May 22.

articles.title: Zuckerberg, Altman, other Big Tech moguls among attendees at Trump-Xi dinner
articles.summary: President Trump hosted Chinese President Xi Jinping at the White House for a state dinner Thursday, whose guest list is full of tech billionaires and some of the world’s most powerful business leaders. Dressed in black tuxedoes, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg, OpenAI co-founder Sam Altman, Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk and Amazon founder Jeff…
articles.body:
President Trump hosted Chinese President Xi Jinping at the White House for a state dinner Thursday, whose guest list is full of tech billionaires and some of the world’s most powerful business leaders.

Dressed in black tuxedoes, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg, OpenAI co-founder Sam Altman, Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk and Amazon founder Jeff Bezos were among the corporate elite invited to attend the dinner, according to a guest list released by the White House.

The dinner capped a day of pageantry and diplomacy for Xi’s visit to Washington, where the two leaders confronted tensions over trade, artificial intelligence and Taiwan before turning to the ceremonial side of the state visit.

Trump had already touted the demand for an invitation to the highly anticipated dinner earlier in the week.

“Everyone wants to be there,” Trump said during the United Nations General Assembly. “It’s the hottest ticket in town.”

When asked who made the cut, Trump said the guest list stretched across corporate America.

“Sort of everybody,” he said, adding that it included “the entire tech world, the entire banking world and a lot more.”

The final list includes dozens of executives from Silicon Valley, Wall Street and other major industries, alongside members of Trump’s Cabinet, lawmakers, Supreme Court justices, media figures and several of Trump’s family members.

The heavy presence of technology executives, including Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, came as competition over AI and advanced computer chips loomed over Xi’s visit.

Nvidia and other U.S. chipmakers have been caught in the crossfire between Washington’s efforts to curb China’s access to advanced technology and the enormous Chinese market.

Trump and first lady Melania Trump, who opted for a tuxedo-inspired look with an oversized bow, greeted Xi and his wife, Peng Liyuan, at the White House before the dinner.

Other industry leaders on the guest list include Google and Alphabet CEO Sundar Pichai, Paramount Skydance CEO David Ellison and former Apple CEO Tim Cook.

Billionaire Bernard Arnault, CEO of the French luxury goods company LVMH which owns major fashion brands including Louis Vuitton and Christian Dior, was accompanied by his son, Alexandre Arnault.

Supreme Court Justices John Roberts, Amy Coney Barrett and Brett Kavanaugh were also on the guest list.

The dinner was held in the White House East Room, with the meal served on fine china dating back to the Reagan administration.

articles.title: Trump praises US-China friendship at state dinner with Xi Jinping
articles.summary: The two superpowers seek greater dialogue despite differences over issues such as Iran, Taiwan, AI and trade.
articles.body:
United States President Donald Trump has thrown China’s leader Xi Jinping a state dinner featuring a tech-heavy guest list, as well as a number of billionaires, Washington powerbrokers, business leaders and the type of festivities that most excite Trump, who has a reputation for reveling in hosting parties.

The dinner on Thursday night wrapped up a day of talks between the two leaders. The summit, Xi’s first visit to Washington in more than a decade, is the second meeting this year between the leaders of the world’s two biggest economies.

Earlier on Thursday, Trump touted what he described as a “great meeting” with Xi, as the two superpowers seek greater dialogue despite differences over issues such as Iran, Taiwan, AI and trade.

“President Xi and I both understand we represent different systems, but the ties between our people endure, and we’ve never gotten along better,” Trump said during his toast on Thursday night, The Associated Press news agency reported.

“Together, we can continue to build a relationship that promotes prosperity and security for future generations,” Trump added.

Trump has done his best to impress Xi during the Chinese leader’s three-day visit to Washington, and the US president praised their close personal relationship — even as he has decried top Democratic candidates as “communists” ahead of the November midterm elections.

Xi and Trump discussed tensions over Taiwan, trade and artificial intelligence during business hours, all while a First Amendment fight over press access at the White House was unfolding. But Trump publicly chose to focus on showing Xi his White House updates on Thursday afternoon, including letting him tour his Marine One presidential helicopter and a new helipad he built for it, before attention quickly turned to the flashy details of the swanky meal.

At one point, Trump invited dinner guests to tour the site of the new ballroom he is building nearby. Construction projects are a frequent digression for a president who has put a lot of focus on remaking Washington’s physical infrastructure.

Xi noted in his own toast that “President Trump has pledged to make America great again” and that “China is committed to achieving great national rejuvenation”.

“These two goals are both ambitious and can surely be mutually reinforcing,” Xi said.

Those who attended included OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, Amazon founder Jeff Bezos, Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and French luxury goods company LVMH CEO Bernard Arnault.

The dinner came after the president took the unusual step of personally greeting Xi and his wife on Wednesday as they arrived at Joint Base Andrews outside Washington. Normally, presidents wait for their guests to arrive at the White House itself before offering a formal welcome.
