articles.title: Why Trump gave Xi an eagle statue at White House state dinner
articles.summary: From redwood benches to DVDs, gifts are an important part of the art of diplomacy.
articles.body:
US President Donald Trump has presented Chinese President Xi Jinping with a sculpture of a bald eagle, a bird native to North America and his country's national symbol, during a lavish state dinner in Washington.

The gift, which was unveiled before VIP guests at the Thursday dinner, embodies "the free and soaring spirit of America", said Trump .

He said that he and First Lady Melania Trump participated in its design. The statue is part of a valuable - but sometimes tricky - aspect of international diplomacy: gift-giving.

Such gifts are a small but meaningful element of the larger aim of Xi and Trump's three-day summit – forging personal relationships between heads of two global superpowers.

"They're going to discuss all of these complicated issues," Daniel Kritenbrink, partner at The Asia Group says. "But at the end of the day, these are still two human beings.

"So that personal relationship means something," he says. "I think the gift exchange is one key part of that."

Kritenbrink, who spent over 30 years as a US diplomat, mostly in Asia, says personal relationships are of particular importance to Xi.

He believes the direct Trump-Xi bond is the glue that is holding together "the most complex and the most consequential relationship in the world".

He says Trump, too, values what Kritenbrink calls "leader-level diplomacy".

Gifts have had a unique presence in the Trump presidency.

The US president has received a luxury jumbo jet, an engraved gold bar, a diamond-and-jewel encrusted gold ring, and more.

Ole Jacob Sending from the Norwegian Institute of International Affairs says: "You think about the Trump presidency in that way, I think gift giving, certainly broadly defined, is very much part of how he operates."

On Thursday morning, Xi announced a gift of two Chinese pandas to a zoo in Atlanta - and a new student exchange programme, which will welcome 100,000 US students to study in China over five years.

"The giant panda have been an envoy of friendship between the Chinese and the Americans," Xi said. "In a few days, two pandas - Ping Ping and Fu Shuang - will come to their new home in Zoo Atlanta and meet with the American people."

It's unclear if he gave any further presents. The BBC has contacted the White House.

Today, the practice of giving lavish gifts mostly exists in Gulf states and autocratic governments.

"Autocracies like China give much more expensive gifts," says Morten Skumsrud Anderson, who co-authored a study on diplomacy and gifts with Sending.

In the West, Anderson says, the tradition has been watered down by democratic guardrails and restrictions.

For example, the US Constitution has an emoluments clause that puts a dollar-value limit on gifts a president can receive from a foreign government.

Currently, the limit is $525 (£397). Anything higher and it becomes federal property, unless the president chooses to buy it back with his own money.

Also, when giving a gift beyond a certain amount, a US president would have to go through Congress, unless he was paying for it personally.

"There are a lot of rules and protocols involved," Sending says, "A lot of thought and process relating to what type of gift to to give, where should the gift exchange happen? How should it happen? When?

"All of this is highly scripted, and involves negotiation at lower levels that goes on for weeks and weeks in advance," Sending says.

Anderson adds: "This is not a last-minute purchase at the airport."

During Xi's state visit to the US in 2013, then-President Barack Obama gifted him an inscribed bench made of redwood, native to California where the two had met. They sat on it together afterwards, smiling for cameras.

It was a more shining example than in 2009, when then-British Prime Minister Gordon Brown gifted Obama an ornamental desk pen holder made from the timbers of a historic anti-slave ship; while Obama gave Brown a set of DVDs, which reportedly were not formatted for UK DVD players.

"That's one example of a kind of an embarrassing exchange," Sending says.

Fortunately, Brown and Obama were allied leaders and not deep rivals looking to resolve seemingly intractable differences.

"You don't want to mess up," Sending says, adding that the wrong gift could potentially derail any larger objectives.

In this case, there is potentially a lot at stake between Trump and Xi.

Their third face-to-face encounter since the start of Trump's second term, this summit is happening amid growing fears of an AI-led apocalypse as both countries race for dominance in the quickly growing industry.

It's also taking place in the wake of a bitter US-China trade war that has only been resolved by a temporary truce, extended on this trip.

So, do the military plane flyovers, cue the performances, fill the wine the glasses, Kritenbrink says. Exchange the gifts.

"It's protocol and it's optics and it's gift giving all as a means to an end, which is stable US-China relations," Kritenbrink says.

"I'll take a fragile truce over a white-hot trade war any day of the week."

articles.summary: Gov. Mikie Sherrill said Lt. Gov. Dale Caldwell’s “ethical lapses persisted despite multiple warnings and trainings.”
articles.body: New Jersey Gov. Mikie Sherrill said Thursday evening that she gave Lt. Gov. Dale Caldwell “until tomorrow” to resign after an investigation found he had violated state ethics and harassment policy. “Today, I’m announcing the conclusion and findings of an independent investigation into allegations regarding Lieutenant Governor Dale Caldwell,” Sherrill wrote on X. “The investigation found that the Lieutenant Governor engaged in serious, repeated violations of state policy and failed to uphold the responsibilities of his office. I’m calling for his resignation and giving him until tomorrow to do so.” The state said this month that it had hired a law firm to investigate allegations against Caldwell, a Democrat who was elected on the ticket with Sherrill last year, claiming that he had behaved inappropriately toward women. Sherrill said Caldwell’s “ethical lapses persisted despite multiple warnings and trainings.” “The substantiated finding of sexual harassment is extremely troubling. I’ve seen firsthand how a hostile culture can undermine everyone’s ability to succeed. It’s insidious and ruptures the trust within an organization,” she said. Sherrill said that the investigation “fully examined the evidence, followed the facts, and protected everyone’s privacy” and that Caldwell’s resignation “is necessary and in the best interest of New Jersey residents.” Lawyers for Caldwell, who has denied the allegations, said in a statement Thursday night that they “strongly disputed the three findings in the investigation,” as its conclusions “go further than the evidence supports.” “This unnecessarily protracted and one-sided process lacked the requisite due process that should be afforded every citizen of this state,” said Thomas Calcagni, a lawyer for Caldwell. Calcagni said Caldwell was “not provided a meaningful opportunity to address each of these anonymous allegations or offer readily identifiable witnesses who possessed more pertinent, first-hand knowledge of the events in question.” The 61-page report found that Caldwell sexually harassed a young female staffer and her friend. Caldwell was also found to have violated state ethics rules for using his office to try to promote a state employee whom he had a romantic relationship with “on multiple occasions,” without disclosing the relationship. He also violated ethics rules by making a practice of taking personal guests to ticketed events without providing payment or reimbursement for the tickets, the report said. State Senate Republican Leader Anthony M. Bucco said in a statement Thursday that the investigation’s findings were “deeply disappointing.” “This situation has gone on for far too long, and if he doesn’t agree to resign, the Legislature should follow the necessary protocols to resolve this matter once and for all,” Bucco said. Caldwell is only the fourth lieutenant governor in New Jersey history, as the role was established by referendum in 2005. It includes the responsibility of taking over as governor when the governor is away, which Caldwell has done numerous times since the investigation began. Caldwell is also New Jersey’s secretary of state, overseeing elections, a critical role as the midterm elections approach in November.

articles.title: UMass Dartmouth football murder suspect overstayed tourist visa, received deferred action: federal sources
articles.summary: Chukwunonso Eze entered the U.S. on a tourist visa in 2015 and received deferred action under both Biden and Trump before he allegedly killed a UMass Dartmouth football player.
articles.body: A Nigerian national accused of killing a UMass Dartmouth football player entered the U.S. on a tourist visa and overstayed it before receiving deferred action under both the Biden and Trump administrations, multiple federal law enforcement sources told Fox News. Chukwunonso Uzoma David Uzoma Eze is charged with murder in connection with the stabbing death of UMass Dartmouth football player Marvins Antoine, 19, during an altercation in Providence, Rhode Island, over the weekend. A second player, Kensley Macean, 19, suffered stab wounds to his head and neck and was taken to Rhode Island Hospital, according to the Providence Police Department. Sources told Fox News that Eze first entered the U.S. on a B-2 tourist visa in 2015. INDIAN NATIONAL ACCUSED OF ARIZONA GIRLFRIEND'S MURDER ENTERED US ON STUDENT VISA: FEDERAL SOURCES Eze received two extensions on his visa under the Obama administration before remaining in the country after his authorized stay expired, according to the sources. Sources said the Biden administration approved Eze's request for deferred action in September 2022. He applied for deferred action again in February 2025 and October 2025, with the latter request approved under the Trump administration on Oct. 8, 2025, according to the sources. Deferred action is a discretionary decision by the federal government to temporarily delay an individual's removal from the United States. It does not provide lawful immigration status. DHS said Eze applied for employment authorization in August 2023, but the request was rejected the following month. ‘CRIMINAL ALIEN’ DUO CHARGED IN DEADLY CONNECTICUT HOME INVASION AS DHS MOVES TO YANK GREEN CARDS He applied again for employment authorization in February 2025 based on deferred action, and DHS said that application remains pending. If convicted of murder, Eze will lose his deferred action, according to DHS. According to Providence police, the stabbing took place at about 12:30 a.m. Saturday in the parking lot outside Mezzo Lounge. Police said the incident stemmed from an altercation involving people who had been inside the lounge before the stabbing. Antoine was killed after a stab to the chest, while Macean suffered stab wounds to his head and neck. articles.title: US and China must act as responsible powers together, Xi says as Trump toasts friendship at state dinner
articles.summary: Trump said he and Xi had "never gotten along better" as he hosted the Chinese president at the lavish White House event.
articles.body:
US President Donald Trump welcomed China's President Xi Jinping to the White House for a lavish state dinner where both leaders touted a new chapter in their friendship.

Xi said the countries "must act as responsible major countries to meet the expectations of our peoples" while Trump toasted a future of "harmony, peace and success" for both nations.

While both pledged to ensure stability between them, experts have cautioned Xi's visit is yet to yield obvious progress on pressing issues.

Billionaire business leaders, Trump administration officials and US tech CEOs were among the dinner's guests. Their arrival was marked, however, by protesters shouting from just outside, some of whom were arrested.

Addressing those gathered late on Thursday, Trump thanked Xi for making the long trip to the US, and said the relationship between the two men was strong.

"We've never gotten along better," Trump said.

He praised the long history of US-China relations, although he did take an unscripted detour to praise his ongoing ballroom project.

In the off-the-cuff moment, he said as a "special treat" the Chinese leader and his wife could be the first to enter the ballroom, which is still a year away from completion.

Xi visit to Washington all pomp but little progress so far

Trump and Xi come face-to-face as US and China battle to win the AI race

"Anybody who wants to walk into a construction site that's nice and clean and sparkling, it's our honour to have you do so," he said.

He also presented Xi with a sculpture of a bald eagle, America's national symbol, saying it embodied "the free and soaring spirit of America".

"We hope it will find a nice, wonderful place in Beijing. It's your honour," he said.

Trump added that he and First Lady Melania had participated in the design of the sculpture.

Xi meanwhile thanked his hosts for receiving him and his wife with "meticulous care and consideration", making them "feel truly at home".

He said the two leaders were "making history in our bilateral engagements".

"We agreed to build a constructive China-US relationship of strategic stability," Xi said, adding that the two shared "sincere and in-depth exchanges" that would strengthen relations between the two countries.

Like Trump's, Xi's remarks were heavy on flattery, focusing on cultural ties and shared history between the US and China.

The relationship between the two countries was "forged in blood and fire" during the fight against Japan in World War Two, before being furthered during the "ping pong" diplomacy of the Nixon administration, he said.

Towards the end of his speech, Xi said the US and China's goals could be "mutually reinforcing". He urged both sides to explore a "new approach for major countries to get along".

When the BBC entered the dining hall for the dinner, SpaceX CEO Elon Musk was standing over a table and appeared to be telling an entertaining story that had two others nearby barreled over with laughter.

Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth was at another table, with a serious look on his face. His wife is sat beside him, with Jared Kushner and White House chief of staff Monica Crowley nearby.

The White House invited scores of US officials, as well as conservative broadcasters, tech industry bosses, social media CEOs and other corporate executives.

Attendees included members of Trump's cabinet, as well as family members like his children Ivanka, Eric and Tiffany.

Bosses from the tech industry in attendance included Apple's Tim Cook, OpenAI's Sam Altman, Google's Sundar Pichai, Amazon's Jeff Bezos and Nvidia's Jensen Huang.

Both Cook and Huang were seated at the same table as Trump and Xi. As was Musk, who previously worked in Trump's administration leading the effort to shrink government.

Other companies whose leaders were in attendance include General Motors, Visa, Paramount Skydance, ExxonMobil and more.

Social media mogul Mark Zuckerberg also attended, as well as Jeff Yaas, the American billionaire who owns a share of TikTok.

"Everybody wanted to be there," Trump said ahead of the event. "I would say you have the entire tech world, the entire banking world, and a lot more."

But one notable absence was Anthropic - one of the biggest and most valuable AI firms in the world. The BBC has asked Anthropic if it was invited, or if they chose not to be there.

The office of the First Lady Melania Trump, which planned the event, said the dinner menu would showcase "American ingredients with subtle Chinese influence".

For their first course guests enjoyed yellow squash, wild mushrooms and crispy pancetta. The ate off red tablecloths - red being a symbol of luck and good fortune in China.

For their main course they dined on a sesame-crusted sea bass, braised bok choy and roasted eggplant.

Dessert featured the two leaders and their fellow diners tucking into vanilla crémeux with sour cherry confit, with an accompanying ice cream "made with harvested White House honey".

The wine chosen by the first lady included Schramsberg Blanc De Noir - a nod to President Nixon's 1972 "Toast to Peace" with former Chinese Premier Zhou Enlai, when they used a bottle from the same vineyard.

Trump and Xi will begin their day with tea at the White House's Red Room with their wives.

The group then head to the US National Archives for a tour of the building and its exhibits.

Formally called the National Archives and Records Administration, the building holds some of the most important documents regarding the founding of the United States - including the US Constitution, the Declaration of Independence and the Bill of Rights.

Xi and his wife will depart Washington later in the day.
